verses.t: [Hermione, Electra, Chorus]
O virgin, art thou come from crowning Clytæmnestra's tomb, and pouring libations to her manes?
I am come, having obtained her good services; but some terror has come upon me, on account of the noise in the palace, which I hear being a far distance off the house.
But why? There have happened to us things worthy of groans.
Speak good words; but what news dost thou tell me?
It has been decreed by this land, that Orestes and I die.
No, I hope not so; you, who are my relations.
It is fixed; but we stand under the yoke of necessity.
Was the noise then in the house on this account?
For falling down a suppliant at the knees of Helen, he cries out--
Who? for I know no more, except thou tellest me.
The wretched Orestes, that he may not die, and in behalf of me.
For a just reason then the house lamented.

For on what other account should one rather cry out? But come, and join in supplication with thy friends, falling down before thy mother, the supremely blest, that Menelaus will not see us perish. But, O thou, that receivedst thy education at the hands of my mother, pity us, and alleviate our sufferings. Come hither to the trial; but I will lead the way, for thou alone hast the ends of our preservation.
Behold I direct my footstep toward the house. Be preserved, as far as lies in me.
O ye in the house, my dear warriors, will ye not take your prey?
Alas me! who are these I see?
(advancing) Thou must be silent; for thou art come to preserve us, not thyself.

Hold her, hold her; and pointing a sword to her neck be silent, that Menelaus may know, that having found men, not Phrygian cowards, he has treated them in a manner he should treat cowards. What ho! what ho! my friends, make a noise, a noise, and shout before the palace, that the murder that is perpetrated spread not a dread alarm among the Argives, so that they run to assist to the king's palace, before I plainly see the slaughtered Helen lying weltering in her blood within the house, or else we hear the report from some of her attendants. For part of the havoc I know, and part not accurately.

With justice came the vengeance of the Gods on Helen. For she filled the whole of Greece with tears on account of the ruthless, ruthless Idean Paris, who brought the Grecian state to Ilium. But be silent, for the bolts of the royal mansion resound, for some one of the Phrygians comes forth, from whom we shall hear of the affairs within the house, in what state they are.
